findings:
Revision 3 fixes all eleven problems from the second review, and none of the first review's thirteen has come back. The numbers were re-checked against the code and by simulation. Two blocking problems remain, both in how the Mine Layer picks and commits to its next line in Open Space; earlier reviews missed them.
- **Standing player:** if the player is standing still, the Mine Layer never commits to a line. Its target point turns with it, so it circles the player until a 6 s give-up fires.
- **Moving player:** if the player flies faster than about 150 px/s, the "lay across the path ahead" calculation keeps pushing the target further away, so the line almost never gets laid ahead. One of the plan's own test rows therefore cannot pass.

Both fixes are local changes to the Mine Layer's planning section and one task's test rows; the design itself is sound:
- fix the player's bearing when the approach starts;
- use the Bomber's existing "earliest reachable time" search instead of the self-referencing formula;
- state honestly that a cruising player gets a fence line behind or beside them, not across their path.

Four small clarifications follow.

| # | Severity | Problem | Fix | Tasks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | blocking | Against a standing player the run-in point turns with the layer's own bearing. The layer can get no closer to it than 450 px, never the 200 px it needs to commit. Every pass waits out the 6 s give-up while circling through earlier mine lines. | Latch the bearing when the approach starts. Add a row: a standing player gets a committed plan within 2.5 s and no fallback. | t11 |
| 2 | blocking | The lead time depends on the distance to the run-in point, which depends on the lead time. Against a 220 px/s player the target sits about 4 km away. The plan commits after 21 s (ahead) or never (abeam or behind), so the "layer ahead → no give-up" control row fails. | Use the Bomber's earliest-feasible scan, and go straight to the fence plan when no arrival is feasible. Move the lead and control rows to about 100 px/s. Say in the summary that a cruising player gets a fence line. | t11 |
| 3 | minor | The plan does not say when "fly to the run-in point" hands over to the run-in, nor that LAY starts on *crossing* the start point. Read the other way, the line comes out up to 66° crooked or starts mid-line. | Hand over within 60 px of the run-in point, and start LAY when the ship crosses the start point from the run-in side. | t11 |
| 4 | minor | For a moving player, the "spread the lines apart" rotation shifts the line about 385 px sideways, so it misses the player's predicted track. | Rotate only the standing-player fence, shift a moving player's line along their heading instead, or state the miss as intended. | t11 |
| 5 | minor | The Bomber's mine scene sets an 8 s life, and the plan keeps it "unless authored". Placed proximity mines (about 40% of the hub field) would then fizzle after 8 s, against the "never fizzles" row. | Placed mode always sets its own life (0 = never fizzles). | t2, t8, t14 |
| 6 | minor | The Mine Layer's exit "along its current heading" in Assault is held in by the corridor constraint unless it is released, so the exit probe would measure a cap rather than an exit. | Call `release_constraint()` in DISENGAGE, as the Bomber does. | t10, t15 |

### 1. A standing player: the plan never commits (blocking)
R = P + 320f − 450u with f re-read every tick from the layer's own bearing, so R always sits 54.6° of bearing ahead of the layer, 552 px from the player. The layer can get no closer to R than 552·sin 54.6° ≈ 450 px. The subagent simulated four starting velocities: the closest approach was 450.1 px, there was no freeze in 12 s, and the layer circled the player at about 330 px.

Consequences:
- every pass against a loitering player is a 6 s give-up;
- the layer flies through its own earlier lines;
- the line rate drops to about one per 20 s;
- §2.18's "2.2 s to reach R" premise is false.

Fix: latch f at APPROACH start until the plan freezes or |v̄| ≥ 60, which gives a freeze in about 1.5 s. Add the row "standing stub, 600 px standoff → frozen ≤ 2.5 s, `fence_fallbacks` 0".

### 2. A moving player: the lead diverges (blocking)
`t_lead` contains |R − pos| / max_speed, and R moves forward with `t_lead`. With a 220 px/s player against a 240 px/s layer, a self-consistent R needs |R − pos| ≳ 4.2 km. Phase 4 hit the same thing (DECISIONS.md:1626, "a plain fixed-point iteration diverged") and solved it with `bomber_brain.gd`'s earliest-feasible scan.

Simulated freeze times for a layer starting 600 px from the player:

| Player speed | Layer ahead | Layer abeam | Layer behind |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100 px/s | 1.5 s | 3.9 s | 8.4 s |
| 150 px/s | 2.9 s | 8.1 s | 15 s |
| 220 px/s | 21 s | never | never |

So the control row (220 px/s, layer ahead, 0 fallbacks) fails, the lead row passes only from a pre-frozen start, and the Gradual 220 px/s scenario is all give-ups.

Fix:
- Use the Phase 4 scan: T in 0.1 s steps up to a cap, then bisect.
- With no feasible T, go straight to the frozen fence plan.
- Put the lead row, the control row and the Gradual moving scenario at about 100–120 px/s, and keep the give-up row at 220 px/s.
- Tell the owner (summary and §5) that a cruising player gets a fence line, not one across their path.

### 3. Run-in handover (minor)
If the run-in starts on freeze, up to 200 px from R:
- a perpendicular arrival reaches 39.6° (bound 40°);
- a freeze from 600 px reaches 66°;
- a "projection ≥ S" test can start LAY mid-line.

Specify the handover within `path_lookahead` 60 px of R, and LAY on crossing S from the R side. Every case tried then stays within 33° and 31 px.

### 4. Spread rotation for a moving player (minor)
At freeze, |C − P| ≈ 1136 px, so θ ≈ 19.8° and C moves about 385 px sideways. That is more than the 300 px half-line, so the predicted track misses the line by about 85 px. Rotate only the fence form, or state this as intended.

### 5. Placed mines and `mine_life` (minor)
`mine.tscn` authors `mine_life = 8.0`. §2.1's "0 unless authored" therefore keeps 8 s on placed PROXIMITY mines, which breaks §2.10's "never fizzles" row and makes the hub field decay. Add a `placed_life` export (default 0), or have `Minefield` zero `mine_life` on its mines.

### 6. DISENGAGE and the corridor constraint (minor)
`AssaultCorridorConstraint` pushes a ship back in past `hard_band` 450, and the exit probe starts head away from the nearest edge. §2.11 needs the line "DISENGAGE calls `mover.release_constraint()`", as the Bomber's does.
